units.en: He often took as principle: "Lead only with punishments and people stay out of trouble but feel no shame."
units.literal: He constantly took as principle "If you regulate them with punishments, the people avoid them but have no sense of shame."

units.zh: 吏人有過，但用蒲鞭罰之，示辱而已，終不加苦。
units.en: For minor faults he swatted offenders with a soft rattan whip—enough to shame them, never to injure.
units.literal: When clerks and people had faults, he only used a rattan whip to punish them—displaying shame only—in the end did not add suffering.

units.zh: 事有功善，推之自下。
units.en: When something went well he credited his subordinates.
units.literal: When affairs had merit and goodness, he pushed them from below.

units.zh: 災異或見，引躬克責。
units.en: When omens appeared he blamed himself first.
units.literal: When disasters or prodigies sometimes appeared, he drew himself in and overcame with self-blame.

units.zh: 每行縣止息亭傳，輒引學官祭酒及處士諸生執經對講。
units.en: Touring his counties he halted at post stations and convened local scholars and students for classical discussion.
units.literal: Whenever traveling counties he stopped to rest at courier stations—always summoned education officials, libationers, and recluses and students holding classics to face one another in lecture.

units.zh: 見父老慰以農裏之言，少年勉以孝悌之訓。
units.en: He urged elders with talk of farming and instructed youths in filial piety and brotherly duty.
units.literal: Seeing elders he consoled them with words of farming hamlets; to youths he exhorted with teachings of filiality and fraternal duty.

units.zh: 人感德興行，日有所化。
units.en: Moved by his virtue, people improved day by day.
units.literal: People felt virtue and arose in conduct; daily there was transformation.

units.zh: 靈帝初，征拜太中大夫，傳講華光殿。
units.en: Early in Emperor Ling's reign he became Grand Counselor of the Palace and lectured on the classics at Huaguang Hall.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ling he was summoned and appointed Grand Counselor of the Palace; lectured by transmission at Huaguang Hall.

units.zh: 遷侍中，賜衣一襲。
units.en: Promoted to Palace Attendant and gifted a full set of robes.
units.literal: Promoted to Palace Attendant; granted one suit of clothes.

units.zh: 轉屯騎校尉，遷宗正，轉光祿勛。
units.en: He rotated through Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and Chamberlain for Palace Attendants.
units.literal: Transferred to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry; promoted to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan; transferred to Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.

units.zh: 熹平五年，代許訓為太尉。
units.en: In Xiping 5 he succeeded Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xiping he replaced Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 靈帝頗好學藝，每引見寬，常令講經。
units.en: Emperor Ling loved scholarship and often summoned Liu Kuan to expound the canon.
units.literal: Emperor Ling rather liked learning and arts; whenever summoning audience with Kuan he regularly ordered him to expound the classics.

units.zh: 寬嘗於坐被酒睡伏。
units.en: Once during an audience he nodded off drunk.
units.literal: Kuan once at sitting was soaked with wine and slept prone.

units.zh: 帝問：『太尉醉邪？』
units.en: The emperor asked whether the Grand Commandant was drunk.
units.literal: The emperor asked, "Is the Grand Commandant drunk?"

units.zh: 寬仰對曰：『臣不敢醉，但任重責大，憂心如醉。』
units.en: Liu answered, "I am not drunk—but my burden weighs so heavily that worry feels like wine."
units.literal: Kuan looked up and replied, "Your servant does not dare be drunk; only the burden is heavy and responsibility great—worry is like drunkenness."

units.zh: 帝重其言。
units.en: The emperor respected his candor.
units.literal: The emperor valued his words.

units.zh: 寬簡略嗜酒，不好盥浴，京師以為諺。
units.en: Liu lived plainly, loved wine, and seldom bathed—the capital turned those habits into jokes.
units.literal: Kuan was plain and negligent and fond of wine; did not like washing or bathing—capital took it as proverb.

units.zh: 嘗坐客，遣蒼頭市酒，迂久，大醉而還。
units.en: Once when hosting guests he sent a servant for wine; the man returned late and roaring drunk.
units.literal: Once entertaining guests he sent a gray-haired servant to buy wine; after a long delay very drunk he returned.

units.zh: 客不堪之，罵曰：『畜產。』
units.en: The guests lost patience and shouted "beast!"
units.literal: Guests could not endure it; they cursed saying, "Livestock."

units.zh: 寬須臾遣人視奴，疑必自殺。
units.en: Liu immediately sent someone to check on the servant, fearing he might harm himself.
units.literal: Kuan shortly sent someone to look at the slave—suspecting he must kill himself.

units.zh: 顧左右曰：『此人也，罵言畜產，辱熟甚焉！
units.en: Turning to his attendants he said, "They insulted a fellow human by calling him cattle—that wound cuts deep.
units.literal: Looking to left and right he said, "This is a human being—curse words calling him livestock—how extreme the insult!

units.zh: 故吾懼其死也。』
units.en: That is why I feared he might take his own life."
units.literal: Therefore I fear his death."

units.zh: 夫人欲試寬令恚，伺當朝會，裝嚴已訖，使侍婢奉肉羹，翻汙朝衣。
units.en: His wife once tried to provoke him: on a court day, after he had dressed, she had a maid spill stew on his ceremonial robes.
units.literal: His wife wished to test Kuan and make him angry; waiting until court assembly; dressing complete; she ordered a serving maid to bring meat stew—overturning and defiling court robes.

units.zh: 婢遽收之，寬神色不異，乃徐言曰：『羹爛汝手？』
units.en: The maid panicked; Liu's expression never changed as he asked softly whether she had burned her hand.
units.literal: The maid hastily gathered it; Kuan's expression was no different; then slowly said, "Did the stew burn your hand?"

units.zh: 其性度如此。
units.en: Such was his temperament.
units.literal: Such was his nature and degree.

units.zh: 海內稱為長者。
units.en: All the empire honored him as a gentleman of true stature.
units.literal: Within the seas he was called a man of mature virtue.

units.zh: 後以日食策免。
units.en: Later a solar eclipse prompted his dismissal.
units.literal: Later owing to solar eclipse he was dismissed by edict.

units.zh: 拜衛尉。
units.en: He was appointed Commandant of the Guards.
units.literal: Appointed Commandant of the Guards.

units.zh: 光和二年，復代段颎為太尉。
units.en: In Guanghe 2 he again succeeded Duan Jiong as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the second year of Guanghe again replaced Duan Jiong as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 在職三年，以日變免。
units.en: After three years another celestial anomaly cost him the post.
units.literal: In office three years; owing to solar anomaly dismissed.

units.zh: 又拜永樂少府，遷光祿勛。
units.en: He then served as Privy Treasurer of Yongle Palace and again as Chamberlain for Palace Attendants.
units.literal: Again appointed Privy Treasurer of Yongle; promoted to Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.

units.zh: 以先策黃巾逆謀，以事上聞，封逯鄉侯六百戶。
units.en: For having anticipated the Yellow Turban plot and reported it, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lu township with six hundred households.
units.literal: Because beforehand he had planned against Yellow Turban rebellion—reported the affair upward—enfeoffed Marquis of Lu township with six hundred households.

units.zh: 中平二年卒，時年六十六。
units.en: He died in Zhongping 2 at sixty-six.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongping he died; at that time aged sixty-six.

units.zh: 贈車騎將軍印綬，位特進，謚曰昭烈侯。
units.en: The court posthumously honored him as General of Chariots and Cavalry with advanced rank and the title Marquis Brilliant and Stern.
units.literal: Posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry seal and ribbon; rank specially advanced; posthumous title Marquis Brilliant and Severe.

units.zh: 子松嗣，官至宗正。
units.en: His son Liu Song inherited the title and rose to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: Son Song succeeded; office reached Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 贊曰：卓、魯款款，情愨德滿。
units.en: The historian praises Zhuo Mao and Lu Gong for their steadfast sincerity and overflowing virtue.
units.literal: The eulogy says: Zhuo and Lu were earnest and sincere—emotion sincere, virtue full.

units.zh: 仁感昆蟲，愛及胎卵。
units.en: Their benevolence touched even insects and spared creatures in the egg.
units.literal: Humane influence moved insects; love reached embryos and eggs.

units.zh: 寬、霸臨政，亦稱優緩。
units.en: Liu Kuan and Wei Ba governed with the same gentle forbearance.
units.literal: Kuan and Ba facing governance likewise were called lenient and slow.

units.zh: 《琴道》一篇未成，肅宗使班固續成之。
units.en: The essay The Way of the Zither was unfinished; Emperor Zhang told Ban Gu to complete it.
units.literal: One piece, The Way of the Zither, was not completed; Emperor Suzong ordered Ban Gu to continue and complete it.

units.zh: 元和中，肅宗行東巡狩，至沛，使使者祠譚塚，鄉里以為榮。
units.en: During Yuanhe, Emperor Zhang toured east to Pei and sent envoys to sacrifice at Huan Tan's tomb—a glory for his hometown.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe period, when Emperor Suzong traveled east on inspection hunt to Pei, he sent envoys to sacrifice at Tan's tomb; the village and neighborhood took it as honor.

units.zh: 章帝七八年间，郡县大螟伤稼，语在《鲁恭传》，而纪不录也。
units.en: Zhang's mid-reign saw caterpillar plagues—Lu Gong's memoir treats them, though the basic annals omit the entry.
units.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Emperor Zhang commanderies and counties had great stem-borers injuring the crops—the account is in the biography of Lu Gong, but the annals do not record it.

units.zh: 時焉子範為左中郎將，誕治書御史，璋為奉車都尉，皆從獻帝在長安，
units.en: His sons held court rank in Chang’an with Emperor Xian: Fan as left general of the gentlemen of the palace, Dan as imperial clerk censor, Zhang as commandant for the imperial chariot,
units.literal: At that time Yan’s son Fan was Left General of the Gentlemen of the Palace, Dan was imperial clerk censor, and Zhang was Commandant of the Chariots; all followed Emperor Xian at Chang’an,

units.zh: 獻帝使璋曉諭焉，焉留璋不遣。
units.en: The emperor sent Liu Zhang west to reason with his father; Liu Yan kept him and never let him return.
units.literal: Emperor Xian sent Zhang to enlighten and instruct Yan; Yan detained Zhang and did not send him back.

units.zh: 《漢獻帝春秋》曰：漢朝聞益州亂，遣五官中郎將牛亶為益州刺史；
units.en: The Annals of Emperor Xian records: Learning of the turmoil, the court dispatched Niu Dan, general of the household for all purposes, as inspector of Yizhou;
units.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian of Han says: the Han court heard that Yizhou was in chaos and sent General of the Household for All Purposes Niu Dan as inspector of Yizhou;

units.zh: 董卓部曲將李傕、郭汜、樊稠、張濟等反，攻京師。
units.en: Li Jue, Guo Si, Fan Chou, Zhang Ji, and other officers of Dong Zhuo’s old army turned on the capital.
units.literal: Dong Zhuo’s division commanders Li Jue, Guo Si, Fan Chou, Zhang Ji, and others rebelled and attacked the capital.

units.zh: 三年春正月丁丑，大赦天下。
units.en: On dingchou in the first month of the third year a general amnesty was granted.
units.literal: In the third year, spring, first month dingchou, he issued a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

units.zh: 秋七月，司空种拂免，光祿大夫濟南淳于嘉為司空。
units.en: In the seventh month Chong Fu left the ministry of works; Chunyu Jia of Jinan, grandee of brilliant candidacy, replaced him.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Chong Fu was dismissed, and Grandee of Brilliant Candidacy Chunyu Jia of Jinan was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 李傕等並自為將軍。
units.en: Li Jue and his confederates each proclaimed themselves general.
units.literal: Li Jue and the others together styled themselves generals.

units.zh: 六月戊午，陷長安城，太常种拂、太僕魯旭、大鴻臚周奐、城門校尉崔烈、越騎校尉王頎並戰歿，吏民死者萬餘人。
units.en: On wuwu the rebels stormed Chang’an; Chong Fu, Lu Xu, Zhou Huan, Cui Lie, and Wang Qi died fighting, and over ten thousand soldiers and civilians perished.
units.literal: On wuwu of the sixth month, they took Chang’an city; Minister of Ceremonies Chong Fu, Grand Coachman Lu Xu, Grand Herald Zhou Huan, Commandant of the Gates Cui Lie, and Colonel of the Agile Cavalry Wang Qi all died in battle; clerks and commoners who died were more than ten thousand.

units.zh: 九月，李傕自為車騎將軍，郭汜後將軍，樊稠右將軍，張濟鎮東將軍。
units.en: In the ninth month Li Jue took the rank of general of chariots and cavalry, Guo Si became general of the rear, Fan Chou general of the right, and Zhang Ji general who guards the east.
units.literal: In the ninth month, Li Jue personally became General of Chariots and Cavalry, Guo Si General of the Rear, Fan Chou General of the Right, and Zhang Ji General Who Guards the East.

units.zh: 李傕殺司隸校尉黃琬，甲子，殺司徒王允，皆滅其族。
units.en: Li Jue murdered Huang Wan, the metropolitan commandant; on jiazi he killed Wang Yun, the minister of education, and exterminated both men’s families.
units.literal: Li Jue killed Metropolitan Commandant Huang Wan; on jiazi he killed Minister of Education Wang Yun, both exterminating their clans.

units.zh: 世祖下詔曰：「武王克殷，表商容之閭，閎修善謹敕，兵起，吏民獨不爭其頭首。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu decreed: "King Wu of Zhou honored Shang Rong's lane after conquering Shang; Wang Hong lived prudently and well, so that when rebellion broke out no mob tried to kill him for sport.
units.literal: Shizu issued an edict saying: "When King Wu conquered Yin, he marked Shang Rong's lane; Hong cultivated goodness and was restrained; when armies rose, clerks and people alone did not vie to take his head.

units.zh: 以《魯詩》教授楚國，龔勝、捨師事焉。
units.en: He taught the Lu recension of the Classic of Songs in the state of Chu; Gong Sheng and Gong She became his disciples.
units.literal: By the Lu version of the Classic of Songs he instructed the state of Chu; Gong Sheng and She took him as teacher to serve.

units.zh: 二十七年，以高等入代趙憙為太僕。
units.en: In year 27, rated highly, he entered court to succeed Zhao Xi as Grand Coachman.
units.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, by high grade he entered court to replace Zhao Xi as Grand Coachman.

units.zh: 和帝时，侍中贾逵荐尤有相如、杨雄之风，召诣东观，受诏作赋，拜兰台令史。
units.en: Emperor He’s attendant Jia Kui likened him to Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong; summoned to the Eastern Lodge for commissioned fu, he became Orchid Terrace clerk.
units.literal: Under Emperor He, Palace Attendant Jia Kui recommended You as having the manner of Xiangru and Yang Xiong; summoned to the Eastern Lodge, ordered to compose fu, appointed Orchid Terrace clerk.

units.zh: 其冬，代尹勤為司空。
units.en: That winter he succeeded Yin Qin as Minister of Works.
units.literal: That winter he replaced Yin Qin as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 孝哀皇帝，元帝庶孫，定陶恭王子也。
units.en: Emperor Ai was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.
units.literal: Emperor Ai (posthumous title Filial-Lamenting) was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.

units.zh: 贊曰：孝哀自為藩王及充太子之宮，文辭博敏，幼有令聞。
units.en: Appraisal: Emperor Ai, from his time as a feudal king to his tenure as Crown Prince, displayed extensive and nimble literary skills, earning an excellent reputation from his youth.
units.literal: Appraisal says: Filial and Lamented, from being a feudal king and filling the position of Crown Prince, had broad and quick literary compositions, from youth had excellent reputation.

units.zh: 上怪之，以問定陶王，對曰：「令，諸侯王朝，得從其國二千石。
units.en: The emperor found this strange and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they are allowed to bring officials ranked at two thousand bushels from their domains.
units.literal: The emperor was surprised by this and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they may bring officials of two thousand bushels from their fiefs.

units.zh: 成帝由此以為不能，而賢定陶王，數稱其材。
units.en: From this, Emperor Cheng concluded that the King of Zhongshan was incompetent, but he came to admire the King of Dingtao and often praised his talents.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng thereby considered the King of Zhongshan incapable, but esteemed the King of Dingtao and frequently praised his abilities.

units.zh: 明年，使執金吾任宏守大鴻臚，持節徵定陶王，立為皇太子。
units.en: The following year, Emperor Cheng sent Colonel Ren Hong, temporarily serving as Grand Herald, to summon the King of Dingtao with imperial credentials and establish him as Crown Prince.
units.literal: The next year, he sent Colonel of the City Gates Ren Hong, acting as Grand Herald, bearing credentials to summon the King of Dingtao and establish him as Crown Prince.

units.zh: 四月丙午，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟。
units.en: In the fourth month, on the day bingwu, the Crown Prince ascended the throne as emperor and performed the ancestral rites at the imperial temple.
units.literal: In the fourth month, on the day Bingwu, the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne and paid respects at the High Temple.

units.zh: 號曰陳聖劉太平皇帝。
units.en: The title shall be Emperor Taiping of the Chengsheng Liu.
units.literal: The title shall be Emperor Taiping of the Chengsheng Liu.

units.zh: 六月戊午，帝崩于未央宮。
units.en: In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, the emperor died in the Weiyang Palace.
units.literal: In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, the emperor passed away in the Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 五月丙戌，立皇后傅氏。
units.en: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, he installed Lady Fu as empress.
units.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Bingxu, he established Empress Fu.

units.zh: 元延四年入朝，盡從傅、相、中尉。
units.en: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (9 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyan, he came to court, his tutor, chancellor, and commandant all accompanying him.

units.zh: 綏和二年三月，成帝崩。
units.en: In the third month of the second year of the Suihe era (7 BCE), Emperor Cheng died.
units.literal: In the third month of the second year of Suihe, Emperor Cheng passed away.

units.zh: 建平元年春正月，赦天下。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the first year of the Jianping era (6 BCE), a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Jianping, he granted amnesty to all under heaven.

units.zh: 二年春三月，罷大司空，復御史大夫。
units.en: In the third month of spring of the second year, the office of Grand Minister of Works was abolished and the Censor-in-Chief was restored.
units.literal: In the third month of spring of the second year, he abolished the Grand Minister of Works and restored the Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 侍詔夏賀良等言赤精子之讖，漢家曆運中衰，當再受命，宜改元易號。
units.en: Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others cited the prophecy of the Red Essence Child, saying that the Han dynasty's ordained fortune was in decline and should receive the Mandate anew, and that the era name and imperial title ought to be changed.
units.literal: Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others spoke of the prophecy of the Red Essence Child: the Han house's ordained fortune was in mid-decline and should receive the Mandate anew; the era name and imperial title ought to be changed.

units.zh: 以建平二年為太初元將元年。
units.en: Let the second year of Jianping be the first year of Taichu Yuanjiang.
units.literal: Let the second year of Jianping be the first year of Taichu Yuanjiang.

units.zh: 三年春正月，立廣德夷王弟廣漢為廣平王。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the third year, King Yi of Guangde's younger brother Guanghan was installed as King of Guangping.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, he established King Yi of Guangde's younger brother Guanghan as King of Guangping.

units.zh: 四年春，大旱。
units.en: In the spring of the fourth year, a severe drought occurred.
units.literal: In spring of the fourth year, great drought.

units.zh: 二月，封帝太太后從弟侍中傅商為汝昌侯，太后同母弟子侍中鄭業為陽信侯。
units.en: In the second month, the emperor enfeoffed the Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin, Chamberlain Fu Shang, as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's younger uterine brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.
units.literal: In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.

units.zh: 元壽元年春正月辛丑朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: In the first year of the Yuanshou era, on the new moon of the first month, day xinchou, there was a solar eclipse.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanshou, on the new moon of the first month, day xinchou, there was a solar eclipse.

units.zh: 丁巳，皇太太后傅氏崩。
units.en: On the day dingsi, Grand Empress Dowager Fu died.
units.literal: On the day dingsi, Grand Empress Dowager Fu passed away.

units.zh: 二年春正月，匈奴單于、烏孫大昆彌來朝。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the second year, the Xiongnu chanyu and the Wusun great kunmi paid court visits.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, the Xiongnu Chanyu and Wusun Great Kunmi came to court.

units.zh: 年三歲嗣立為王，長好文辭法律。
units.en: At the age of three, he succeeded as king, and as he grew up he came to favor literary composition and the study of law.
units.literal: At age three he succeeded to the throne as king, and when grown he favored literary compositions and laws.

units.zh: 成帝亦自美其材，為加元服而遣之，時年十七矣。
units.en: Emperor Cheng himself admired the young man's talents, performed the coming-of-age capping ceremony for him, and sent him back home. He was seventeen at the time.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng himself admired his abilities, performed the capping ceremony for him, and sent him away; he was then seventeen years old.

units.zh: 秋九月壬寅，葬義陵。
units.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on the day renyin, he was interred in the Yiling tomb.
units.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, on the day renyin, he was buried in the Yiling tomb.

units.zh: 詔曰：「漢興二百載，曆數開元。
units.en: An edict stated: "The Han has risen for two hundred years, and the cycle of fate opens a new beginning.
units.literal: An edict stated: "The Han has risen for two hundred years; the cycle of fate opens a new beginning.

units.zh: 即位痿痺，末年寖劇。
units.en: Upon ascending the throne, he suffered from paralysis; in his later years, the condition steadily deteriorated.
units.literal: Upon ascending the throne he had flaccid paralysis; in his final years it gradually worsened.

units.zh: 睹孝成世祿去王室，權柄外移，是故臨朝婁誅大臣，欲彊主威，以則武、宣。
units.en: Witnessing how in Emperor Cheng's era, hereditary stipends left the imperial family and power shifted to outsiders, he frequently executed ministers upon ascending the throne, seeking to strengthen imperial authority and emulate Emperors Wu and Xuan.
units.literal: He observed that in the generation of Filial Cheng, emoluments departed from the imperial house, authority shifted outward, therefore upon ascending the throne he frequently executed ministers, desiring to strengthen imperial authority, to follow Wu and Xuan.

units.zh: 雅性不好聲色，時覽卞射武戲。
units.en: His refined character showed no interest in music or sensual pleasures; he occasionally enjoyed watching archery contests and martial demonstrations.
units.literal: His elegant nature did not favor music and sex; he occasionally viewed archery and martial displays.

units.zh: 傅、相、中尉皆國二千石，故盡從之。」
units.en: The tutor, chancellor, and commandant are all two-thousand-bushel officials in my domain, so I brought them all with me.'
units.literal: The tutor, chancellor, and commandant are all officials of two thousand bushels in the state, so I brought all of them.'

units.zh: 上曰：「朕聞夫婦一體。
units.en: The emperor declared: 'I have heard that husband and wife are one flesh.
units.literal: The emperor said: 'I have heard that husband and wife are one body.

units.zh: 《詩》云：『穀則異室，死則同穴。』
units.en: The Book of Odes states: "In life they occupy different rooms, in death they share one grave."
units.literal: The Odes say: "While alive they dwell in separate chambers, in death they share the same tomb."

units.zh: 昔季武子成寑，杜氏之殯在西階下，請合葬而許之。
units.en: In ancient times, when Ji Wuzi had completed his funeral preparations, the coffin of his wife from the Du family lay at the western steps. He requested joint burial and was granted permission.
units.literal: Formerly Ji Wuzi completed his sleeping arrangements, the Du family's coffin was at the western steps, he requested joint burial and it was permitted.

units.zh: 附葬之禮，自周興焉。
units.en: The practice of joint burial originated with the Zhou dynasty.
units.literal: The rite of joint burial arose from the Zhou dynasty.

units.zh: 『郁郁乎文哉！
units.en: 'How elegant and civilized!
units.literal: 'How cultured and refined!

units.zh: 吾從周。』
units.en: I shall follow the Zhou tradition.'
units.literal: I follow the Zhou.'

units.zh: 孝子事亡如事存。
units.en: A dutiful son honors the dead as he would honor the living.
units.literal: A filial son serves the deceased as if serving the living.

units.zh: 帝太后宜起陵恭皇之園。」
units.en: The Imperial Empress Dowager should be buried in the grounds of Emperor Gong's tomb.'
units.literal: The Imperial Empress Dowager should have her tomb raised in Emperor Gong's park.'

units.zh: 謝曰：「臣幸得繼父守藩為諸侯王，材質不足以假充太子之宮。
units.en: He respectfully declined, saying: 'I am fortunate to have succeeded my father in holding my fief as a feudal king. My talents and character are inadequate to serve even temporarily as Crown Prince.
units.literal: He declined, saying: 'Your servant has fortunately succeeded his father in guarding the border as a feudal lord king. My abilities and qualities are insufficient to temporarily fill the position of Crown Prince.

units.zh: 陛下聖德寬仁，敬承祖宗，奉順神祇，宜蒙福祐子孫千億之報。
units.en: Your Majesty's wisdom and benevolence are boundless. You honor your ancestors and obey the gods, and surely you will be blessed with countless descendants.
units.literal: Your Majesty's sage virtue is broad and benevolent; reverently continuing the ancestors, complying with the spirits, you should receive blessed protection for your descendants numbering thousands and myriads.

units.zh: 臣願且得留國邸，旦夕奉問起居，俟有聖嗣，歸國守藩。」
units.en: I wish only to remain in my residence for now, serving you faithfully by inquiring daily about your well-being, until you have a worthy heir, and then return to guard my domain.'
units.literal: I wish to remain in my country's residence for now, morning and evening attending to your inquiries about your condition, awaiting a sage heir, then return to my country to guard the border.'

units.zh: 書奏，天子報聞。
units.en: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor acknowledged it.
units.literal: The memorial was presented; the Son of Heaven acknowledged receipt.

units.zh: 詔曰：「春秋『母以子貴』，尊定陶太后曰恭皇太后，丁姬曰恭皇后，各置左右詹事，食邑如長信宮、中宮。」
units.en: An imperial edict declared: 'As the Spring and Autumn Annals teach, "The mother gains honor through her son." The Empress Dowager of Dingtao shall be honored as Empress Dowager Gong, and Lady Ding as Empress Gong. Each shall have their own attendants, with estates equal to the Changxin Palace and the imperial residence.'
units.literal: An edict stated: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals say "The mother is honored through the son." Honor the Empress Dowager of Dingtao as Empress Dowager Gong, and Lady Ding as Empress Gong. Each shall have left and right palace attendants established, with fiefs equal to the Changxin Palace and the Central Palace.'

units.zh: 六月，詔曰：「鄭聲淫而亂樂，聖王所放，其罷樂府。」
units.en: In the sixth month, an imperial edict declared: 'The decadent music of Zheng confuses proper ritual music; the sage kings banished it. We shall abolish the Music Bureau.'
units.literal: In the sixth month, an edict stated: 'Zheng music is licentious and confuses ritual music; the sage kings banished it. We shall abolish the Music Bureau.'

units.zh: 詔曰：「河間王良喪太后三年，為宗室儀表，益封萬戶。」
units.en: An imperial edict declared: 'King Liang of Hejian mourned his mother for three years, setting an example for the entire imperial clan. His fief shall be increased by ten thousand households.'
units.literal: An edict stated: 'King Liang of Hejian mourned his empress dowager for three years, serving as a model for the imperial clan. His fief shall be increased by ten thousand households.'

units.zh: 又曰：「制節謹度以防奢淫，為政所先，百王不易之道也。
units.en: Another edict declared: 'Controlling expenditures and maintaining proper standards to prevent extravagance and immorality is the highest priority in governance. This is the eternal principle followed by all wise rulers.
units.literal: Another edict stated: 'Moderating expenditures and being careful with standards to prevent extravagance and licentiousness is the foremost matter in governing. It is the unchanging way of the hundred kings.

units.zh: 諸侯王、列侯、公主、吏二千石及豪富民多畜奴婢，田宅亡限，與民爭利，百姓失職，重困不足。
units.en: Feudal kings, marquises, princesses, high officials, and wealthy families accumulate vast numbers of slaves and servants, owning unlimited fields and estates. They compete with ordinary people for profits, leaving the common folk unemployed and suffering from severe poverty.
units.literal: Feudal lords, marquises, princesses, officials of two thousand bushels, and wealthy commoners extensively accumulate slaves and bondservants, fields and dwellings without limit, contending with the people for profit. The common people lose their occupations, suffering doubly from hardship and insufficiency.

units.zh: 其議限列。」
units.en: Let the officials discuss and establish proper limits.'
units.literal: Let there be discussion of establishing limits.'

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕承宗廟之重，戰戰兢兢，懼失天心。
units.en: An imperial edict declared: 'I bear the sacred trust of our ancestral temples, filled with trepidation, fearing lest I lose Heaven's favor.
units.literal: An edict stated: 'I bear the heavy responsibility of the ancestral temples, trembling with fear, afraid of losing the favor of heaven.

units.zh: 間者日月亡光，五星失行，郡國比比地動。
units.en: Recently, the sun and moon have been eclipsed, the five planets have wandered from their proper paths, and earthquakes have struck repeatedly throughout the commanderies and principalities.
units.literal: Recently the sun and moon have lost their light, the five planets have deviated from their courses, and earthquakes have occurred repeatedly in commanderies and states.

units.zh: 乃者河南、穎川郡水出，流殺人民，壞敗廬舍。
units.en: Recently, flooding in Henan and Yingchuan commanderies has drowned people and destroyed homes and shelters.
units.literal: Recently in Henan and Yingchuan commanderies water overflowed, flooding and killing people, destroying houses and dwellings.

units.zh: 朕之不德，民反蒙辜，朕甚懼焉。
units.en: My lack of virtue has caused the people to suffer unjustly; I am deeply alarmed by this.
units.literal: Because of my lack of virtue, the people have conversely suffered unjustly; I am greatly fearful.

units.zh: 已遣光祿大夫循行舉籍，賜死者棺錢，人三千。
units.en: I have dispatched an Imperial Household Grandee to tour the affected areas and register the victims, granting three thousand cash for coffins to each of the dead.
units.literal: I have already dispatched an Imperial Household Grandee to tour and register them, granting coffin money to the dead, three thousand cash per person.

units.zh: 其令水所傷縣邑及他郡國災害什四以上，民貲不滿十萬，皆無出今年租賦。」
units.en: Order that counties and towns damaged by flooding, and other commanderies and states where disaster losses reach four-tenths or more, and where people's property is less than one hundred thousand cash, shall all be exempted from this year's rents and taxes.'
units.literal: Order that counties and towns damaged by water and other commanderies and states suffering disasters of four-tenths or more, people whose property is less than one hundred thousand, all shall not pay this year's rents and taxes.'

units.zh: 二月，詔曰：「蓋聞聖王之治，以得賢為首。
units.en: In the second month, an imperial edict declared: 'It is said that wise rulers prioritize finding worthy officials above all else.
units.literal: In the second month, an edict stated: 'I have heard that the governance of sage kings takes obtaining worthy men as the first priority.

units.zh: 其與大司馬、列侯、將軍、中二千石、州牧、守、相舉孝弟惇厚能直言通政事，延于側陋可親民者，各一人。」
units.en: Together with the Grand Commandant, marquises, generals, and officials of all ranks, let them recommend individuals who are filial and brotherly, sincere and upright, able to speak frankly and understand governance, including those from humble backgrounds who can connect with the people - one person each.'
units.literal: Let them together with the Grand Commandant, marquises, generals, officials of middle two thousand bushels, provincial governors, governors, and chancellors recommend filial and fraternal, sincere and substantial, able to speak directly and understand state affairs, extending to those in humble positions who can be close to the people, each one person.'

units.zh: 夏四月，詔曰：「漢家之制，推親親以顯尊尊。
units.en: In the fourth month of summer, an imperial edict declared: 'The Han dynasty system honors relatives to demonstrate respect for superiors.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer, an edict stated: 'The Han system promotes kinship to manifest respect for superiors.

units.zh: 定陶恭皇之號不宜復稱定陶。
units.en: The title of Emperor Gong of Dingtao should no longer include the name Dingtao.
units.literal: Emperor Gong of Dingtao's designation should not again be called Dingtao.

units.zh: 尊恭皇太后曰帝太太后，稱永信宮；
units.en: Empress Dowager Gong shall be honored as Imperial Grand Empress Dowager, residing in the Yongxin Palace;
units.literal: Honor Empress Dowager Gong as Imperial Grand Empress Dowager, called the Yongxin Palace;

units.zh: 恭皇后曰帝太后，稱中安宮。
units.en: Empress Gong shall be honored as Imperial Empress Dowager, residing in the Zhong'an Palace.
units.literal: Empress Gong shall be called Imperial Empress Dowager, called the Zhong'an Palace.

units.zh: 立恭皇廟于京師。
units.en: A temple for Emperor Gong shall be established in the capital.
units.literal: Establish Emperor Gong's temple in the capital.

units.zh: 赦天下徒。」
units.en: All prisoners throughout the empire shall be granted amnesty.'
units.literal: Grant amnesty to convicts throughout the realm.'

units.zh: 八月，詔曰：「時詔夏賀良等建言改元易號，增益漏刻，可以永安國家。
units.en: In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others proposed changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.
units.literal: In the eighth month, an edict stated: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Helang and others proposed changing the era name and designation, increasing the water clock periods, believing it could permanently secure the state.

units.zh: 朕過聽賀良等言，冀為海內獲福，卒亡嘉應。
units.en: I erroneously heeded the words of Helang and his associates, hoping to bring blessings to the entire realm, but ultimately received no favorable signs.
units.literal: I mistakenly listened to Helang and others' words, hoping to obtain blessings for all within the seas, but in the end there was no auspicious response.

units.zh: 皆違經背古，不合時宜。
units.en: All these proposals violate the classics and contradict ancient precedents, failing to suit the current era.
units.literal: All of these contravene the classics and oppose antiquity, not conforming to what is appropriate for the times.

units.zh: 六月甲子制書，非赦令也，皆蠲除之。
units.en: The imperial order issued on the jiazi day of the sixth month was not a pardon; all such measures are to be rescinded.
units.literal: The edict of the jiazi day in the sixth month was not an amnesty decree; all of them are to be remitted and eliminated.

units.zh: 賀良等反道惑眾，下有司。」
units.en: Helang and his associates defy moral principles and mislead the people; turn them over to the authorities.'
units.literal: Helang and others go against the Way and delude the masses; send them to the officials.'

units.zh: 皇天降非材之佑，漢國再獲受命之符，朕之不德，曷敢不通！
units.en: Heaven has sent protection to one unworthy such as I; the Han state has again received the token of the Mandate. My virtue is inadequate — how dare I not comply!
units.literal: Heaven has sent protection unworthy of one such as I; the Han state has again received the token of the Mandate. My virtue is inadequate — how dare I not comply!

units.zh: 夫基事之元命，必與天下自新，其大赦天下。
units.en: In founding matters of primal mandate, one must renew oneself together with all under Heaven. Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm.
units.literal: In founding matters of primal mandate, one must renew oneself with all under Heaven. Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm.

units.zh: 漏刻以百二十為度。」
units.en: The clepsydra gradations shall take one hundred twenty as the standard."
units.literal: The clepsydra gradations shall take one hundred twenty as the standard."

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕獲保宗廟，不明不敏，宿夜憂勞，未皇寧息。
units.en: An edict stated: "I have been able to preserve the ancestral temples, but I am neither enlightened nor quick in understanding. Day and night I labor in anxiety and have had no time for peaceful rest.
units.literal: An edict stated: "I have succeeded in preserving the ancestral temples, yet I am unenlightened and unperceptive; night and day I worry and labor, never at ease.

units.zh: 惟陰陽不調，元元不贍，未睹厥咎。
units.en: Yin and yang are not in harmony, the common people lack sustenance, and I have not seen where the fault lies.
units.literal: Only yin and yang are not in harmony, the common people lack sustenance, and I have not seen where the fault lies.

units.zh: 婁敕公卿，庶幾有望。
units.en: Time and again I have charged the high ministers, hoping for improvement.
units.literal: Time and again I have charged the high ministers, hoping for improvement.

units.zh: 至今有司執法，未得其中，或上暴虐，假勢獲名，溫良寬柔，陷於亡滅。
units.en: Even now, the officials who enforce the law have not found the proper balance. Some exalt the violent and cruel, borrowing power to win a name for themselves, while the gentle, good, lenient, and mild are driven into destruction.
units.literal: Until now the officials enforce the law without hitting the mean: some flatter the violent and cruel and gain reputation by borrowed power, while the mild, good, lenient, and gentle fall into ruin.

units.zh: 是故殘賊彌長，和睦日衰，百姓愁怨，靡所錯躬。
units.en: For this reason, cruelty and harm spread ever further, harmony declines day by day, and the common people grieve and resent, with nowhere to place themselves in safety.
units.literal: Therefore the cruel and harmful grow ever longer, concord daily declines, the hundred surnames grieve and resent, with nowhere to set themselves aright.

units.zh: 乃正月朔，日有蝕之，厥咎不遠，在余一人。
units.en: Now, on the new moon of the first month, the sun has been eclipsed. The fault is not far away; it lies in me alone.
units.literal: Then on the new moon of the first month there was a solar eclipse; the fault is not far off — it lies in me alone.

units.zh: 公卿大夫其各悉心勉帥百寮，敦任仁人，黜遠殘賊，期於安民。
units.en: Let the ministers and grandees each devote his whole heart to encouraging and leading the officials, earnestly appoint humane men, dismiss and keep far away the cruel and harmful, and make the people's security the goal.
units.literal: Let the ministers and great officers each with full heart exhort and lead the hundred offices, earnestly appoint benevolent men, dismiss and keep distant the cruel and harmful, and aim at settling the people.

units.zh: 陳朕之過失，無有所諱。
units.en: Set forth my faults and failings; let none be concealed.
units.literal: Set forth my faults and failings; let none be concealed.

units.zh: 其與將軍、列侯、中二千石舉賢良方正能直言者各一人。
units.en: Together with the generals, ranked marquises, and officials of two thousand bushels, each shall recommend one worthy, upright, and forthright person.
units.literal: Together with the generals, marquises, and officials of two thousand bushels, each shall recommend one person who is worthy, upright, and able to speak frankly.

units.zh: 大赦天下。」
units.en: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
units.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."

units.zh: 昭儀及根見上亡子，亦欲豫自結為長久計，皆更稱定陶王，勸帝以為嗣。
units.en: Consort Zhao and Wang Gen, observing that the emperor had no sons, wanted to secure their own long-term interests. They both spoke highly of the King of Dingtao and urged the emperor to name him as heir.
units.literal: Consort Zhao and Wang Gen, seeing that the emperor had no sons, also wished to secure themselves for the long term, and both spoke favorably of the King of Dingtao, urging the emperor to make him heir.

units.zh: 後月餘，立楚孝王孫景為定陶王，奉恭王祀，所以獎厲太子專為後之誼。
units.en: Over a month later, he installed Jing, grandson of King Xiao of Chu, as King of Dingtao to maintain the sacrifices to King Gong, thereby encouraging the Crown Prince to concentrate solely on securing the succession.
units.literal: More than a month later, he established King Xiao of Chu's grandson Jing as King of Dingtao to continue King Gong's sacrifices, in order to encourage and exhort the Crown Prince to focus single-mindedly on succession.

units.zh: 性疾惡宦官，遂為所陷，靈帝初，與長樂少府李膺等俱以黨事誅。
units.en: He despised the eunuchs and they ruined him; early in Emperor Ling's reign he was executed with Li Ying and others in the faction cases.
units.literal: By nature he hated evil eunuchs; therefore was framed by them; at the beginning of Emperor Ling, together with Prefect of Changle Li Ying and others alike by faction affair executed.

units.zh: 太尉段颎谄附佞幸，宜并诛戮。
units.en: Grand Commandant Duan Jiong had curried favor with the clique and should die with them.
units.literal: Grand Commandant Duan Jiong fawned on the favorites and ought likewise to be executed.

units.zh: 颎亦自杀。
units.en: Duan Jiong killed himself.
units.literal: Jiong also committed suicide.

units.zh: 于是悉收甫、颎等送洛阳狱，及甫子永乐少府萌、沛相吉。
units.en: They seized Wang Fu, Duan Jiong, and their confederates for the Luoyang jail, including Wang Fu’s son Wang Meng, chamberlain for the palace revenues at Yongle, and the chancellor of Pei, Wang Ji.
units.literal: Thereupon all were arrested—Fu, Jiong, and the rest—and sent to the Luoyang prison, together with Fu’s son Meng, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues of Yongle, and Ji, Chancellor of Pei.

units.zh: 前虽纠诛王甫、段颎、盖简落狐狸，未足宣示天下。
units.en: Killing Wang Fu and Duan Jiong only swept aside a handful of foxes; the realm has not yet seen the full reckoning I promised.
units.literal: Though I earlier impeached and executed Wang Fu and Duan Jiong, that was merely like clearing away a few foxes—not enough to proclaim justice to the realm.”
